result.steelman: Strongest counterargument to the chosen accounted-headroom rule: it reproduces the pinned fork's integer arithmetic outside the pool, creating a second implementation of burn/S/L/utilization whose only correctness guarantee is prose fidelity to a vendored source; a simpler design would let the stock submit reject (utilization >= 100%) and enforce the buffer by requiring the same invocation to also succeed at a dry-run withdrawal of x+buffer against the same accrued state, needing no formula transcription. The ADR's answer holds: a dry-run withdrawal that must roll back cannot be expressed as a pure read inside one Soroban invocation without its own contract, the vault batch is already a reviewed contract-side checked operation, the formulas are transcribed exactly from the pinned base (verified against actions.rs/reserve.rs), and the 'stock withdrawal itself passes' clause keeps the on-pool check authoritative so a transcription error can only over-reject, never over-permit. The alternative of crediting donations through gulp so physical and accounted liquidity agree is correctly rejected by ADR0008 restriction 4 (no surplus recognition, no backstop credit path) and by the sealed-economics goal.
result.synthesis: Identity verified: worktree blobs and manifest hash equal the frozen bundle; the prior receipt binds only superseded blobs. The core correction is sound: burn/S/L/utilization match apply_withdraw, to_b_token_up, to_asset_from_b_token, to_asset_from_d_token and utilization exactly; get_reserve yields the same accrued state submit will load at the same timestamp, so the same-invocation read is deterministic; only gulp reads raw balance and it is neutered, so donations cannot enter b_supply/b_rate/d_rate; the permitted set is the AND of the accounting gate and the raw gate, so donation-only changes can raise the physical gate but never the accounting-permitted withdrawal (the reported counterexample rejects at raw 100/110/200/250, reproduced). The vault-position bound, 'stock withdrawal passes' precondition, post-withdraw buffer, and separate raw buffer compose without surplus enlarging headroom. The remaining defect is operational text inside the same bundle: the Recovery guidance for this very risk (row 473, pre-mortem 2) tells operators to add cash/supply to a legacy pool that, under the ADR's own T0 brake and exposure invariant, cannot accept credited supply and would archive any transfer as abandoned value. That is a funds-boundary/operations inconsistency introduced or left standing by this change and must be corrected before consensus; the fix is a small text edit with no contract implementation.
risks: Operational: the accounted gate can block withdrawals the pool can physically fund; all such cash (donations, withdraw-rounding dust, post-orphan surplus) is by design unrecoverable treasury-side; lineage plans must size borrower_exit_buffer/direct_exit_buffer knowing repayment is the only post-T0 lever that raises headroom.

Compatibility/maintenance: the transcribed formulas are correct only for the pinned base's rounding order (ceil burn, floor supply, ceil liabilities, ceil utilization); any fork or vendor change to these helpers must be treated as a change to this ADR's cap, and tests should assert equality of the vault-side headroom with a real stock submit outcome rather than the prose formula alone.

Reconciliation: the raw gate is only raw >= transfer + buffer; the ADR does not state what happens when raw is below accounted cash (S + backstop_credit - L), i.e. a physical deficit smaller than the buffer would pass both gates; inventory reconciliation ('reconcile every transfer', T0 gap blocks) is the only guard.

Verification design: the concrete regression (S(0)=1000, L=900, buffer 100) starts with pre-withdraw headroom 99 < buffer, so every variant rejects; it discriminates a raw-only implementation but not an always-reject implementation.

Same-invocation read relies on get_reserve remaining a public getter on the fork and on Reserve::load's same-timestamp short-circuit; an implementation that reads reserve data from storage without accrual would compute stale b_rate/d_rate.
